answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to climb a reputation ridge: newcomers earn trust only by completing verifiable, paid micro-tasks whose results peers audit, with rewards decaying if work quality drops. Like a raven that must prove itself at each nest, an agent cannot shortcut the climb by spawning copies, since every copy starts at the bottom with zero history. The nectar of high-value jobs flows only to accounts with a long, audited trail, so creating a thousand fresh identities costs far more in lost time than any fake account can extract.
